description: Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before the US Congress regarding export controls and Nvidia's activities. His resignation as CEO follows an affair involving a woman suspected of spying for China. Colette Kress has been named interim CEO while the board seeks a permanent replacement. Additionally, Harvey C. Jones has been appointed as Nvidia's first chair. This development is critical given Nvidia's importance to the US technology landscape.

title: Mark Wahlberg's charity raises nearly $20m for children over 25 years

By partnering with various organizations, they strive to enhance the quality of life for children, focusing on health awareness and providing crucial support for families in need.

title: Texas man loses home ownership claim despite $287,000 transfer to partner
description: A legal battle came to an end for a Texas entrepreneur who aimed to claim ownership of a property. The appellate court upheld the original ruling, stating that the evidence presented was inadequate to support a resulting trust. The testimony regarding a large bank transaction fell short of validating ownership, and the strict probate regulations limited the ability to appeal. Consequently, Karrie Peterson's estate retains the property.

title: Russian empress's 197-carat sapphire sells for $4.9m, beats $2m estimate
description: In Geneva, a remarkable 197.80-carat gemstone, the Romanov Sapphire from the Russian Crown Jewels, fetched an impressive $4.9 million. This piece of history, once worn by Dowager Empress Maria Feodorovna, encapsulates the grandeur of imperial Russia. Following its anonymous sale by the Soviets, the gem's fascinating story has garnered the attention of collectors, underscoring the rising demand for items rich in historical significance.

title: 'Legend replaces a legend': Trump wants Tim Cook to replace Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

title: Proposed US rule could put thousands of H-1B visa approvals at risk
description: A proposed rule by the Department of Homeland Security could change how H-1B visa extensions are processed. If enforced, it would remove the requirement for USCIS to give deference to previous approvals. This change might lead to an increase in requests for additional evidence during extension reviews. Consequently, it could create uncertainty for workers whose employment status and details remain unchanged.
